sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics; statutory law supreme and judicial interpretations authoritative)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: All bilateral investment treaties in force between the People's Republic of China and the home jurisdiction of each foreign beneficial owner, evaluated on a case-by-case basis
Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Singapore on the Promotion and Protection of Investments

Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Singapore for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2007, as subsequently amended); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Management (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (Order No. 26 of the President of the People's Republic of China, effective January 1, 2020); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each direct foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies in the shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive route selected solely by origin state: if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member, notarize where required and obtain a Hague Apostille from that state's designated competent authority; if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention member, complete notarization and origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the PRC Embassy or Consulate. The two routes are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence / Status Certificate) of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / corporate affairs authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same parallel exclusive path as above: Hague Apostille only for Apostille Convention members; Consular Legalization only for non-members; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the WFOE and designation of local agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign shareholder / corporate secretary or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same parallel exclusive path: notarize signatures and either obtain a Hague Apostille from a member state or execute the Consular Legalization sequence for a non-member state; mutually exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Association of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered office / corporate records keeper in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same parallel exclusive path: apostille or consular legalization depending solely on originating state membership; no sequential combination of both systems.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the shareholder's commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the shareholder's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank and notary signature authentication, followed by Hague Apostille where the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, or by PRC Consular Legalization where that jurisdiction is not a member; the two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, agents and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Sanctions List, and Chinese government sanctions and export-control prohibition lists; enhanced due diligence applies to foreign and domestic PEPs, including immediate family members and close associates; continuous transaction monitoring, risk scoring, and annual re-screening are mandatory; adverse media hits require written clearance memoranda signed by the AML compliance officer and escalation to the legal and compliance committee before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Self-Declaration Service Platform (online national integrated enterprise registration and name clearance system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE's statutory Chinese name must consist of four tiers in order: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry description, and company form. The trade name must be written in simplified Chinese characters; an English transliteration may be used in contracts and bank filings but has no independent legal effect. Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and foreign scripts are generally not permitted in the trade name unless special approval is granted under the enterprise-name regulation. Phonetic transliteration of a foreign investor's brand is permissible if it is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name and does not contain a prohibited token.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five working days of a name rejection, the applicant should file a written request for the registered reasons through the SAMR portal and simultaneously re-file a modified name declaration. If the modified name is rejected again, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next higher level SAMR authority within 60 days of the refusal. If reconsideration is unsuccessful or not answered, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit before the competent People's Court within six months. A licensed legal advisor must review the rejection reference number, legal grounds, and revised name construction before each re-filing to prevent abusive successive filing sanctions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the registered address of a WFOE for tax registration or bank account opening; the local tax authority and banks require a physical office address evidenced by a notarized Chinese lease agreement and landlord title certificate. Certain government-designated centralized registration addresses in free-trade zones, high-tech parks, and incubator operators are accepted only when the operator issues a venue-use certificate and the WFOE can demonstrate real operational substance. For a low-risk micro-SaaS business, remote work is acceptable, but the registered office must remain accessible for legal service and regulatory inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: current Chinese lease contract with property ownership certificate of the landlord; photograph of the external signboard; floor plan; proof of utility/office equipment; at least one local contact able to receive inspectors. Quantified risk: 15-30% random inspection probability per year for a low-risk WFOE located in a commercial office building; if the registered address is a shared virtual office or incubator address, probability of targeted address verification rises to 60-75%, and failure to demonstrate physical presence can lead to cancellation of tax registration under the Tax Administration Law and Company Law address requirements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication of foreign investor corporate documents (Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing, Board Resolution, Articles, Bank Reference Letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent apostille/legalization authority in the shareholder's state of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the origin jurisdiction plus official apostille/consular fees; default professional handling fee of USD 100 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed translation into simplified Chinese of the authenticated foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed translation agency or notary-affiliated translation service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: RMB 150-250 per A4 page; notary certification of translation per package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: WFOE name clearance and pre-registration declaration support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - zero official name-clearance fee; service fee charged by filing agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory registry fee; agent/document preparation fee at market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company registration application and SAMR filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - no official registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Company Law of the People's Republic of China; Measures for the Administration of Company Registration; no administrative fee; any cost is legal counsel or agent fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal engraving (legal-person seal, financial seal, contract seal, invoice seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized seal-engraving enterprise (public security bureau filing fee included)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local public security tariff schedule and market engraving price

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration and electronic tax-bureau activation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local tax authority (zero official fee) and licensed accountant for e-tax initialization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tax Administration Law registration requirement; service fee per official fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of RMB basic deposit account and foreign-currency capital account at commercial bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank (account tariff) and corporate service agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff schedule for account opening, KYC due-diligence, and administrative handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease legal inspection and landlord document certification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord/property management company and local notary office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market lease benchmark plus notary fee for rent contract and address certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP/sanctions screening, and incorporation legal memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee or hourly billing at USD 150-300 per attorney hour

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23, 24, 27, 32, 33, 34, 35, 38, 40, 46, 47 and 51; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 4 and 31; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746), Chapters II and III
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), Enterprise Registration Bureau, administered locally by the Municipal or District Market Supervision Administration at the registered address of the WFOE
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Establishment Registration and the Articles of Association submitted through the SAMR integrated online service platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory paid-up minimum applies to a WFOE limited liability company engaged in ISIC 6201 software publishing and SaaS services. The governing capital rule is the full subscription and five-year payment-in obligation under Article 47 of the PRC Company Law (2023 Revision). The shareholders must set the registered capital in the Articles of Association, pay subscriptions in RMB through a proper capital account, obtain capital contribution certificates, and no blocked escrow account or deposit certificate is required for information-technology service activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED ENTERPRISE) The undersigned board members of [Company Name] Limited (the Company), a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established under the laws of the People's Republic of China, acting together at the first meeting of the Board of Directors held on the date set forth in the attached minutes, constitute a quorum and adopt the following resolutions: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be fixed at [Registered Address, City], China, and the legal representative shall file the address and all subsequent changes with the appropriate Market Supervision Administration in accordance with the PRC Company Law and market entity registration regulations. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company shall be [Amount] RMB, divided into [Number] ordinary shares with par value of [Amount] RMB each, subscribed as set forth in the Articles of Association. Each shareholder shall pay the subscribed capital in full no later than five years after the date of establishment. The legal representative is authorized to open a designated capital contribution account, issue capital contribution certificates upon payment, and maintain the register of shareholders in accordance with applicable law. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open a RMB basic deposit account and any necessary foreign currency capital account with [Bank Name]. The legal representative, [Name], and the chief financial officer, [Name], are designated as the sole authorized signatories, and the bank is authorized to honor all instructions bearing the signatures of both authorized signatories, or of any two authorized signatories where the Board has expressly approved a dual-signature matrix. This banking authorization remains in force until the Board delivers a written revocation to the bank. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Legal Representative of the Company, [Name] is appointed General Manager, [Name] is appointed Supervisor, and [Name] is appointed Financial Manager. The officers shall hold office until removed by the Board and shall exercise powers and duties described in the Articles of Association and applicable corporate governance rules. RESOLVED, that the legal representative and the general manager, acting jointly, are authorized to execute and submit all filing forms, tax registrations, employment registrations, bank account forms, foreign exchange reporting forms, and any other instruments necessary to carry out the foregoing resolutions and to legally bind the Company to third parties. RESOLVED, that any two of the directors may certify a copy of this resolution, and such certified copy shall be accepted by any governmental authority, bank, accounting firm, or partner as proof of the corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization of Foreign Investor Documents and Enterprise Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Reservation Portal, or the Market Supervision Administration service hall of the intended registered city
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign sole shareholder must first legalize its corporate existence and board resolution. For countries that have joined the Hague Apostille Convention, the documents must be notarized by a local notary, obtain an Apostille certificate, and be translated into Chinese by an accredited translation service. For non-Hague jurisdictions, consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate is mandatory. After the legalization package is ready, the applicant should complete the online enterprise name reservation on the SAMR portal, selecting the limited liability company form, the WFOE structure, the registered city, and the business scope for software development and SaaS services (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210). The result will be an Enterprise Name Pre-Approval Notice, valid for six months, which must be attached to the later establishment application. The legal representative should also verify that the proposed name does not include restricted terms and that no identical properly registered entity exists in the local registration database.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation of the sole foreign shareholder, notarized and apostilled or consularly legalized
Board or shareholder resolution of the foreign investor approving WFOE establishment and the subscribed capital amount
Certified Chinese translation of all foreign legalization documents
Draft Articles of Association of the proposed WFOE
Lease agreement or property ownership certificate for the registered office address
Copy of the passport or corporate ID of the proposed legal representative
Power of attorney and agency incorporation service agreement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, read the rejection reason in the SAMR portal, correct the restricted item, and immediately submit a fresh name application. If the legalization package is deemed defective, obtain a compliant replacement apostille or consular certificate and submit a corrected certified translation before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Establishment Registration Application and Issuance of the Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal or District Market Supervision Administration of the registered address, acting under SAMR, through the integrated online platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the name is reserved, the applicant shall file the Company Establishment Registration package through the SAMR online platform or at a service window. The application includes the executed Articles of Association, shareholder qualifications, the registered office lease, the appointment documents for the legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager, and the Enterprise Name Pre-Approval Notice. The authority will verify the capital subscription, the five-year contribution schedule, the legality of the business scope, the adequacy of the corporate governance structure, and the absence of foreign investment negative-list restrictions. Software and cloud services are not on the negative list and do not require prior approval from the Ministry of Commerce, but the Foreign Investment Information Report should be completed with the same filing. Once approved, the Market Supervision Administration will issue the Business License of Enterprise Legal Person with the Unified Social Credit Code, which serves as the foundation for all subsequent registrations.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Establishment Registration (legally signed by all shareholders)
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Enterprise Name Pre-Approval Notice
Notarized and legalized shareholder qualification documents
Proof of registered address, including lease and landlord property ownership certificate
Appointment documents and identity certificates of the legal representative, supervisor, executive director, and general manager
Foreign Investment Information Report submitted through the SAMR integrated system
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended, the authority will issue a written certificate of need for correction listing the exact defects. The applicant must cure and resubmit through the online rectification channel within the prescribed ten workdays, or withdraw the case and start a fresh filing without penalty. If the business scope description is overbroad or under-described, align the scope text to ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 and the Micro_SaaS subscription commercial model.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Seal Carving, Articles of Association Filing, and Tax Registration Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau designated seal-engraving service; State Taxation Administration tax service hall or Electronic Taxation Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one to two days after the business license is issued, the legal representative must complete the filing of the company official seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal with the local Public Security Bureau. The seal-engraving entity will submit the seal information to the PSB automated filing system and issue a Seal Filing Certificate. Then, using the Unified Social Credit Code on the business license, the company must activate its electronic tax registration by logging into the Electronic Taxation Bureau, confirming the tax type, accounting standards, invoicing status, and general taxpayer election. Since the WFOE is an entity-level taxpayer, the tax registration should be completed before any invoicing. The tax authority will issue the tax registration notices and approve the invoice quota based on the declared business scope. In parallel, the Foreign Investment Information Report is automatically pushed to the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the multi-sector reporting system.
required_dossiers: Business License of Enterprise Legal Person
Identity certificate of legal representative
Seal Carving Authorization or Seal Filing Form
Enterprise name and Unified Social Credit Code notification
Lease contract and landlord property file for tax registration address
Articles of Association and board resolution appointing tax handlers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Security Bureau does not confirm the seal filing, revisit the seal-engraving company to ensure the legal representative ID and business license copies are correctly uploaded. If tax registration is locked, call the taxpayer services hotline to obtain the error code and submit a written explanation through the tax hall, including any correction of the registered address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration, and Capital Injection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Chinese commercial bank such as Bank of China or HSBC China, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) registration function performed through the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must open a RMB basic deposit account and a foreign currency capital account after the license and seal are effective. The legal representative must attend the bank appointment with all corporate paperwork, including the board resolution authorizing banking relationships and the dual-signatory mandate. During the account opening process, the bank will complete the SAFE FDI registration on behalf of the company using the Foreign Investment Information Report, and will assign a Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate. The company should then inject the subscribed capital, either in RMB from abroad or in foreign currency, through the capital account in compliance with the capital account conversion rules. Under the PRC Company Law, all capital must be fully paid in within five years. The bank will also conduct customer due diligence and beneficial ownership verification under the Anti-Money Laundering Rules; the risk tier for a Micro_SaaS service is low, but the bank still requires an updated corporate structure chart.
required_dossiers: Business License and Seal Filing Certificate
Legal representative passport or ID card and second authorized signatory ID
Board resolution approving bank account opening and signatory authority
Articles of Association and certificate of incorporation of the parent company
Foreign Exchange Registration request form completed at the bank
Foreign Investment Information Report acceptance notice from the SAMR and Ministry of Commerce integrated system
Beneficial ownership declaration and corporate structure chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses or delays account opening, obtain a written refusal citing internal policy and apply to another licensed bank. If SAFE registration is rejected, correct the Foreign Investment Information Report and resubmit through the bank under the SAFE record-filing procedure, or apply to the local SAFE branch for manual registration with a written explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board is required because the WFOE performs software publishing and cloud SaaS services under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210, not physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operating permit is required for the consumer micro SaaS business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - pure digital service with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity; no Environmental Impact Assessment filing or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the operation produces no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams. If the company later adds physical facilities, an Environmental Assessment Filing or a higher-tier environmental clearance may become mandatory under the Law on Environmental Impact Assessment and the discharge limits of national pollutant standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for cloud-hosted, serverless SaaS operations. If a conventional office is leased, the landlord should provide the building fire-safety acceptance certificate and the company should comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China regarding fire extinguishers and evacuation routes, but no separate Civil Defense fire permit or industrial occupational clearance is required for pure software activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), with electronic filing through the National Electronic Tax Service Platform (e-Tax Portal) administered by the local competent tax office in the registered jurisdiction of the WFOE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A WFOE is a PRC resident limited liability company. Step 1: incorporate with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Business License, which carries the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), the sole statutory Tax Identification Number used for both EIT and VAT. Step 2: complete tax registration within 30 days of the Business License issuance through the e-Tax Portal; the SAMR data-sharing mechanism automatically creates the taxpayer record. Step 3: choose VAT registrant status; if expected annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000, mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies; below that threshold, small-scale taxpayer treatment is the default, though voluntary general taxpayer registration is permitted. Step 4: for ancillary non-resident withholding obligations (e.g., cross-border royalty payments), register as a withholding agent under the same USCC. Step 5: foreign non-resident suppliers with no PRC establishment may separately apply for a Non-Resident Taxpayer Number at the competent tax office for VAT withholding or direct registration, but that status does not apply to the WFOE itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise subject to Enterprise Income Tax at the statutory 25% rate on its worldwide income; no pass-through or transparent treatment is available under Chinese law. For VAT, the WFOE is either a small-scale taxpayer or a general taxpayer depending on annual turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not operate a check-the-box regime or hybrid mismatch election comparable to the US or OECD-style hybrid rules. A WFOE may elect to be registered as a VAT general taxpayer even below the RMB 5,000,000 threshold, and may elect small-scale taxpayer treatment if it qualifies. No consolidated corporate income tax filing election is available for PRC subsidiaries.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT). The statutory standard goods rate is 13%, while the subject SaaS supply falls under the modern services / information technology services bracket at 6%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (annual taxable sales). Exceeding this threshold makes VAT general taxpayer registration mandatory; below the threshold, the WFOE may remain a small-scale taxpayer and obtain simplified VAT treatment. For cross-border digital services supplied into China by foreign sellers, separate registration or collection duties may apply under the e-commerce VAT collection regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue VAT invoices through the STA-controlled Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice system or the traditional tax-control invoice system. Digital invoices are uploaded in near real-time to the STA database through the e-Tax Portal API; each invoice bears a unique invoice code and inspection number, enabling anti-fraud verification. There is no separate physical fiscal stamp for electronic invoices; paper special VAT invoices require tax-control equipment and must be recorded in the VAT return. All sales and export documents must be reconciled to the invoicing system and the SAFE foreign exchange reporting database before export zero-rating is claimed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical goods, zero-rating applies when goods are lawfully exported from China and the export customs declaration is matched to sales invoices, payment receipts, and foreign exchange collection. For the SaaS service, zero-rating or exemption applies under the PRC cross-border taxable services policy when the software service is supplied to an overseas non-resident enterprise or individual, the service is wholly consumed outside China, and consideration is received from outside China. Payment orchestration by Paddle or Lemon Squeezy does not by itself establish eligibility; the controlling evidence is the subscription contract, overseas consumer or business identity, IP or service delivery logs, and the recorded foreign exchange receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill for physical exports
Foreign exchange collection receipt from the settling bank (functional equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate / FIRC)
Commercial invoice and export packing list (for goods)
Cross-border software subscription agreement or service contract (for SaaS)
Proof of overseas service recipient and service consumption outside mainland China
Payment gateway settlement reports from Paddle or Lemon Squeezy matched to bank remittance records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of export zero-rating are subject to strict STA and SAFE audit. The taxpayer must preserve all underlying export and foreign exchange records for at least five years. If the tax authority determines the zero-rated or refunded VAT was claimed fraudulently or without adequate substantiation, it will claw back the refunded VAT, impose late-payment interest at 0.05% per day, and apply administrative penalties of between 50% and 500% of the tax evaded under the Law on the Administration of Tax Levying and Collection. In serious cases involving false export documents or fictitious cross-border services, criminal liability for VAT fraud and export tax fraud may attach under the Criminal Law, alongside retrospective reclassification of the supply as taxable at 6% or 13% VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) acting as the delegated foreign exchange control and enforcement authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed limited convertibility regime. Current account transactions are generally free of prior approval and legally convertible through designated foreign exchange banks, subject to genuine trade or service background verification and SAFE's cross-border receipt and payment monitoring. Capital account transactions remain strictly controlled: foreign direct investment into a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise requires SAFE registration through the bank, a foreign exchange capital account, and compliance with the negative list access regime. Profit remittances by a WFOE are permitted after annual audit and tax clearance, provided the enterprise has completed capital verification and has no outstanding foreign debt repayment obligations; remittances are processed under current account items as investment income, but banks require board resolutions, tax payment certificates, audited financial statements, and a FATCA/CRS declaration. Surrender requirements for export proceeds have been largely liberalised; enterprises may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign exchange accounts, but receipts must be repatriated into China and, when settled into Renminbi, must be supported by verified trade documents within the reporting timeline. Practical integration with the central bank's cross-border payment and anti-money laundering systems is mandatory, and any discrepancy triggers a bank suspension and SAFE penalty. Therefore, although the current account is de jure convertible, bank-level compliance under the know-your-customer, know-your-business and know-your-documents doctrine creates a quasi-approval process.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange account in China; there is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio for ordinary current account proceeds, as the enterprise may decide to retain the funds in foreign currency or voluntarily settle them into Renminbi with a designated bank. The bank must verify the export declaration, invoice, bill of lading and the China International Trade Single Window data; export receipts should normally be credited within 90 days of goods declaration in the goods trade foreign exchange administration system, and if not matched within the bank's stipulated grace period, a written explanation and supporting logistics evidence are required. Mandatory settlement applies only to specific capital account revenues such as foreign debt drawdowns and foreign direct investment injection quotas, where the registered capital settlement proceeds may be converted at the account bank after capital verification, subject to applicable SAFE pilot zone rules. In practice, for a micro-SaaS exporter, each inbound subscription payment must be reported with a service trade code, and banks apply a one-to-one, item-by-item document matching rule for cross-border service receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account for FDI and Basic Deposit Account in Renminbi

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Common Deposit Account for Operational Renminbi and Foreign Currency Current Account
Cross-border settlement account integrating e-commerce receipts and operational disbursements
Capital escrow account and trade settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech EMIs, including UK- and Hong Kong-licensed e-money institutions, are legally barred from opening domestic bank accounts or holding client funds in Mainland China without a payment institution licence issued by the PBOC. They cannot act as the depository institution for the WFOE's registered capital, cannot obtain SAFE foreign exchange registration, and cannot issue domestic account numbers for Chinese tax invoices. Their only permissible function is as a payment facilitation layer for cross-border platform collections, and even that requires partnership with a licensed Chinese bank or an established e-commerce cross-border payment institution. For treasury purposes, a micro-SaaS WFOE should maintain its primary liquidity and capital accounts in a Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank and use EMIs only for merchant-of-record settlement disbursements where the underlying platform is a foreign acquiring entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is effectively mandatory for first-time corporate account opening at a domestic Tier-1 bank. The legal representative of the WFOE, or a fully authorised senior officer carrying a notarised power of attorney stamped with the corporate common seal and foreign parent company board resolution, must appear in branch for primary identity verification and account activation. Some commercial banks accept a remote notarised proxy opening for a foreign parent through the nearest Chinese consulate when the WFOE is newly formed, but the local bank compliance officer still requires a physical interview with the local finance director or an escrow agent before disbursement privileges are enabled. Video-only KYC is generally accepted for existing clients and for supplementary account signatories, but not for the inaugural account opening due to the PBOC's identity protection and anti-money laundering rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity caused by a multi-tier offshore parent chain above the WFOE
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foreign parent's certificate of incorporation, a full ownership chain chart from ultimate individual shareholders to the WFOE, a notarised certificate of incumbency or company register extract issued within 90 days, passports of all ultimate beneficial owners, and a board resolution authorising the WFOE's opening of banking facilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and funding legitimacy for initial registered capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the parent company for the last two years, six months of parent bank statements showing the source of the remitted capital, sale and purchase agreement or share subscription agreement, a personal source-of-wealth statement and supporting evidence for individual shareholders, plus a declaration of no borrowing or third-party financing without a formal loan agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business purpose mismatch risk where the stated scope is software publishing but the account will receive recurring subscription fees from retail consumers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed product commercialisation narrative, executed SaaS terms of service and privacy policy, merchant-of-record agreements with Paddle or Lemon Squeezy, platform payout reports, the ISIC 6201 classification evidence, and the WFOE's revenue recognition policy demonstrating alignment between the bank's transaction monitoring and the cashflow pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed persons and adverse media screening hits on foreign shareholders or counterparty merchants
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent global watchlist screening reports from an accepted provider covering OFAC, EU, UN and Chinese lists, CPF and position statement for any PEP or family member, adverse media search results with explanations, and a risk-based customer due diligence assessment prepared by the compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign parent remits registered capital from its own account to the WFOE's foreign exchange capital account via SWIFT, using purpose code Foreign Direct Investment or Construction of Enterprises in China in accordance with SAFE's balance-of-payments classification. The remittance must be filed with the PRC bank against the SAFE foreign exchange registration certificate, the company's business licence, the foreign investment information report entry, and the equity subscription documents. Upon arrival, a Chinese certified public accountant performs a capital verification and issues a capital verification report before the enterprise may apply for conversion of the registered capital into Renminbi under the settlement-in-account model. The settlement of registered capital must be used within the permitted business scope, and funds cannot be diverted to entrusted loans, securities investments, or real estate unless expressly permitted by pilot zone rules. For operational funding beyond capital, the WFOE may borrow foreign debt under the macro-prudential formula published by SAFE, with registration and bank-based settlement control.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade settlements for the micro-SaaS business are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 messages for service fees, software royalties, cloud hosting charges and affiliate payouts, with supporting contracts, invoices, service delivery reports and tax withholding vouchers attached to the bank's trade document system. For physical goods ancillary to the software licence, such as hardware API devices or promotional merchandise, the enterprise may use documentary collections or irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued by its Tier-1 bank; however, the most efficient clearing rail for recurring consumer subscription revenue is direct merchant-of-record settlement into the WFOE's foreign currency current account, followed by bank-settled conversion into Renminbi at the prevailing spot rate or a pre-booked forward rate. Trade-related liquidity should be centralised in one foreign currency account to avoid confusing current account with capital account receivables, and each outbound payment must be allocated to the correct balance-of-payments code to avoid triggering false negative-list screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Bank-settled forward foreign exchange contracts for service trade cashflows, with underlying commercial documents and a real trade background verification
Foreign currency swaps between US dollars and Renminbi for tenor-matched match funding of cross-border subscriptions and vendor payments, limited to hedging identified current account exposures
Foreign exchange options purchased from a licensed domestic bank for risk management of cashflow volatility, but not for speculative net open positions

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards may be entered by the foreign parent as a macro hedge of the WFOE's Renminbi exposure, but the WFOE itself cannot freely access NDFs onshore without a genuine cross-border transaction and SAFE authorisation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Information Publicity Report (annual business-license/company annual report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June for the immediately preceding calendar year; no incorporation-anniversary extension applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion on the Enterprise Operating Abnormal List; after three consecutive years without remediation, transfer to the Seriously Untrustworthy Enterprise List, triggering interdepartmental joint-disciplinary restrictions, publicity of violation, enhanced supervision over the legal representative and responsible persons; for a company inactive for six consecutive months without justified reason, the registration authority may revoke the business licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return (annual CIT filing and final tax clearance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) / local tax service offices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May following the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of RMB 2,000 or less, increasing to RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases; late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; for under-reporting or non-payment, administrative penalty of 50% to five times the tax underpaid; enforced collection, tax-collection blacklisting, travel/external-exit restrictions, and ordering of rectification by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (foreign-invested enterprise annual information report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via the joint SAMR/MOFCOM annual-report information system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June for the previous calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative order to rectify within 20 days; failure to do so or making a false/misleading report may expose the enterprise to a fine of up to RMB 200,000, in addition to inclusion in abnormal-operation/monitoring records and delayed processing of foreign-investor changes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Direct Investment Equity Ownership Information Report (SAFE annual equity-interest filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through a designated bank or the SAFE capital-account information system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June after the calendar-year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Recording of the enterprise and its foreign investor in SAFE monitoring/abnormal lists; suspension or restriction of cross-border foreign-exchange receipts, profit remittance, capital account transactions and bank processing until the report is remedied; administrative penalties may also be imposed under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual financial-statement audit by a licensed PRC CPA firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders/board and statutory records; audited financial data must be consistent with the SAMR annual report and the annual CIT return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually following the 31 December balance sheet date and in practice completed in time for the annual CIT return/annual report deadlines, normally by 30 April to 31 May of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company Law violation if the audit is omitted; regulators may order rectification, and directors, supervisors and senior managers may be held liable for losses; a false or omitted statutory audit invalidates lawful profit distributions and blocks lawful foreign-exchange profit remittance by the WFOE, and the CPA firm may be fined or have its licence revoked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social insurance contribution-base declaration and monthly employer contribution filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (HRSS) and social insurance collection agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: National annual deadline is not fixed; the employer must declare the contribution base annually in the local cycle (commonly June-July for the next contribution year) and file/pay monthly.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or under-paid social-insurance contributions incur daily arrears interest at 0.05%, may be forcibly deducted, and may lead to administrative fines, enforcement by the HRSS/collection authority, and legal action by employees; prolonged non-compliance does not itself strike off the company but can block annual administrative clearances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual housing-provident-fund contribution-base declaration and monthly provident-fund remittances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Housing Provident Fund Management Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the local provident-fund adjustment cycle, commonly effective 1 July, with monthly remittances throughout the contribution year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid or under-paid contributions are subject to a supplementary remittance order and daily overdue surcharge, followed by compulsory execution if outstanding; the enterprise can be administratively sanctioned by the local provident-fund authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual individual income tax final-settlement reconciliation support and withholding records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via local tax service offices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employer withholding throughout the year; annual comprehensive-income final settlement for resident employees is made from 1 March through 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold or remit withheld individual income tax makes the employer liable for the underpaid tax plus daily late-payment interest and administrative penalties up to 100% of the amount of tax; serious cases are publicly published and enforced by tax authorities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: China imposes a categorical statutory-audit obligation with no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption for a WFOE limited-liability company: under the PRC Company Law, every company must prepare annual financial reports and have them audited by an accounting firm, irrespective of asset size, revenue, or employee count. The annual SAMR report profiles total assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, and taxes, and the annual CIT filing requires reconciled financial statements; for a foreign-invested micro SaaS company the same mandatory audit applies because of its corporate form, even if the volume of transactions is small.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), which are substantially converged with IFRS; qualifying small enterprises may apply the Simplified PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, but must still prepare Chinese statutory financial statements in RMB and, if applicable, reconcile to the requirements of the annual CIT return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not maintain a public beneficial-ownership register for ordinary domestic WFOEs; AML/CFT customer due-diligence rules require the WFOE to identify beneficial owner(s) with its banks/counterparties and refresh that information within 30 days of any qualifying change. For shareholder transfers, the company must update its shareholder register and apply to SAMR for registration of the equity-transfer change within 30 days from the date the change occurs; any resulting change in foreign investment status or capital structure must also be reported to MOFCOM/SAFE in the applicable 30-day event-reporting window. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation filing to SAMR.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$800-US$6,000 per year in first-tier cities like Shanghai/Beijing/Shenzhen, with lower lease/address costs or registered-agent-type services in second- and third-tier cities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500-US$7,500 per year for a micro WFOE SaaS entity with low transaction volumes; the fee rises with revenue volume, intercompany balances, cross-border royalty services, and consolidation requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 4)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprise (annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, employees not exceeding 300, total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million): taxable income reduced to 25% and applied at 20% rate, resulting in an effective 5% CIT rate. National High-Tech Enterprise: preferential 15% rate. Key software enterprise: two-year exemption, three-year half-rate reduction if software-related revenue and R&D intensity thresholds are met. R&D expenses qualify for a 100% additional super deduction. VAT on qualifying SaaS exports may be zero-rated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 - Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Type A), filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing system (e-Tax)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual final settlement and payment must be filed within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year (for a calendar-year enterprise: by May 31). Quarterly provisional prepayment returns and payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Micro-SaaS subscription sales and related software services (excluding VAT) recognized under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all subscription revenue sourced from China and global customers if the WFOE is a China tax resident. Do not net out platform fees paid to Paddle or Lemon Squeezy; those are deductible operating expenses. Diverting revenue to an offshore entity without genuine local substance will trigger a recharacterization attack.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to providing SaaS services, including cloud infrastructure, hosting, bandwidth, and third-party software license fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capitalized software development costs must be amortized over their useful life. Intercompany purchases of services must satisfy the arm's-length principle. Payments to foreign service providers may create a Chinese permanent establishment if the services are performed in China and are not ancillary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty, and real estate / land use taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate income tax is not deductible. VAT on domestic SaaS revenue is generally 6% (modern services), but software product sales may be 13%; VAT is reported separately on the VAT return and cannot be booked as CIT operating expense. Non-resident digital-service providers may be subject to VAT registration in China if they supply directly to Chinese consumers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses, including marketing, platform commissions, salaries, office rent, professional fees, and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign related parties must be supported by contracts, invoices, evidence of actual service receipt, and TP analyses. Excessive management, trademark, or royalty fees paid to an offshore parent are non-deductible if they lack economic substance. Interest expense on related-party loans is limited by thin-capitalization rules (debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 in general cases, 5:1 for financial enterprises).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit before tax computed under Chinese accounting standards, after operating expenses, non-operating income, and non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the accounting book profit that becomes the base for reconciliation. SaaS deferred revenue from annual subscriptions must be recognized ratably over the subscription term. Cash-basis accounting is not permitted. The WFOE must not deduct dividends to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Lines 14-18 - Tax Adjustments and Loss Carryforwards)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation lines: tax increase adjustments, tax decrease adjustments, tax-exempt and reduced income, additional deductions, overseas taxable income, and prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible entertainment expenses (deduction capped at a statutory ratio), unqualified related-party interest, fines, administrative penalties, and expenses without valid tax invoices. Claim the 100% R&D super deduction for eligible micro-SaaS development. Losses may be carried forward 5 years, or 10 years for high-tech and technology-focused small / medium-sized enterprises. Non-resident shareholders cannot offset WFOE losses against their local taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Lines 19-21 - Taxable Income and Applicable Rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all adjustments and the computed CIT at the applicable rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate, or the 15% preferential rate for a valid High-Tech Enterprise certificate, or the small low-profit enterprise reduced taxable income mechanism resulting in an effective 5% rate. This line does not include dividend withholding tax; outbound dividend WHT is a separate levy imposed on the non-resident shareholder at the time of distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Lines 22-30 - Tax Reductions, Credits, and Net Tax Payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax incentive reductions for low-profit enterprises, foreign tax credit offsets, and any other credits, culminating in net CIT payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit foreign income taxes paid on qualifying foreign-source income, limited to China tax liability on that income. If the WFOE distributes profits to a non-resident parent, the 10% dividend WHT (or lower treaty rate) is not an expense of the WFOE; the WFOE acts as withholding agent and must remit the WHT to the tax authority at the time of payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return triggers a fine of RMB 2,000 under Article 62 of the Tax Administration Law, rising to RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious violations, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under Article 32. Fraudulent under-declaration or tax avoidance under Article 63 is subject to a fine from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. False declarations may also trigger criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, with imprisonment up to 7 years and confiscation of assets for large-scale evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% for dividends paid by a China-resident WFOE to a non-resident enterprise shareholder (Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 3 and 27, and Implementing Regulations Article 91). Treaty rates may reduce the WHT to 5% in many Chinese DTAs when the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% of the paid-in capital, provided substance requirements are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before dividend distribution, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority and complete the non-resident beneficial owner determination required by SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9. The WFOE must submit a treaty benefit application through the e-Tax portal, including ownership structure, proof of beneficial ownership, evidence of core business substance, and a declaration that the recipient is not a conduit. The application must be filed before withholding, or a refund may be claimed within 3 years if the wrong rate was withheld. Tax authorities may deny treaty benefits if the principal purpose is treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax rates for non-residents are 10% on interest and 10% on royalties paid by a China-resident enterprise. Treaty rates vary: for example, under the China-Hong Kong arrangement, dividends are 5% (if 25%+ shareholding), interest 7%, and royalties 7% (industrial property and copyright royalties); many other Chinese DTAs provide a 10% or 5% rate. All treaty relief requires submission of TRC, beneficial ownership proof, and a substantive assessment of the payment underlying the services or IP. Excessive or artificial royalty payments cannot be deducted in China, and interest deductions are subject to thin capitalization limits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: related-party tangible asset transfers exceeding RMB 200 million; related-party intangible asset transfers exceeding RMB 100 million; related-party financial asset transfers exceeding RMB 100 million; and other related-party transactions (services, interest, royalties, commissions) exceeding RMB 40 million in a single tax year. Master File: mandatory when aggregate related-party transactions in the prior tax year exceeded RMB 1 billion. Transactions below thresholds still require an Annual Related Party Transaction Report with the annual CIT filling.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code, but the general anti-avoidance rule (Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47) and the substance-over-form doctrine (Tax Administration Law Article 35) require genuine business purpose and actual economic activity in China. For treaty relief, the OECD-derived beneficial ownership and principal purpose test applies. A WFOE engaged in micro-SaaS must demonstrate that Core Income-Generating Activities - software development, price setting, risk management, customer contracting, and strategic decision-making - are performed or controlled in China, not merely held as passive ownership in a low-tax shell. Any offshore entity claiming income must be able to show real employees, office premises, and operational decision-making consistent with its claimed CIGA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully under-reporting SaaS subscription revenue by routing customer payments through offshore payment processors such as Paddle or Lemon Squeezy without attributing the income to the WFOE, or claiming inflated or fictional R&D expenses to abuse the 100% R&D super deduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration Law: recovery of the underpaid tax plus late-payment interest; fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. Article 201 of the Criminal Law: where the amount evaded is relatively large and exceeds 10% of taxable income, imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine; where the amount evaded is huge and exceeds 30%, imprisonment of 3 to 7 years and a fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil under Company Law Article 20 (and its successor Article 21 in the revised Company Law) if the director abuses the WFOE's separate legal personality to evade tax debts or defraud creditors. Directors who order or knowingly participate in the fraud are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax; their personal assets may be frozen, they may be placed on the tax blacklist, subjected to travel/exit bans, and criminally prosecuted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging above-arm's-length management fees, royalty payments, or interest rates to the offshore parent or related parties, or failing to prepare and submit the Local File, Master File, and Annual Related Party Transaction Report when statutory transaction thresholds are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 41, 44, and 48 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and SAT Announcement [2016] No. 42 authorize the tax authority to assess tax on a deemed basis, adjust related-party income, add interest (with additional adjustment interest if documentation is defective or incomplete), and impose administrative fines for failure to comply with filing obligations. Failure to submit the related-party report may result in a fine of RMB 10,000 or more, and serious cases may be treated as tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation or intentionally hide related-party transactions may be held personally responsible for the resulting tax underpayment under the abuse-of-in-personality doctrine. The tax authority may ask courts to blacklist the director, impose exit restrictions, and attach personal assets. If the TP omission is part of a fraudulent scheme, criminal liability under Article 201 (tax evasion) or Article 162 (collusion to evade tax) could lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Treaty Shopping / Artificial Permanent Establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting a Hong Kong or other offshore shell entity with no employees, office, bank accounts, or decision-making substance to receive SaaS royalties or dividends from the WFOE solely for the purpose of obtaining the reduced 5% dividend withholding or 7% royalty rate and to avoid the full 10% statutory WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will deny treaty benefits under the principal purpose test (OECD BEPS Action 6) and SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9 beneficial ownership rules. The full 10% statutory WHT will be recovered from the non-resident, and the WFOE as withholding agent will be held liable for underwithheld tax plus daily interest under the Tax Administration Law. A fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax may be imposed if the arrangement is deemed fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or structure the abusive shell arrangement can be personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and for assisting in tax evasion, particularly if they control the offshore conduit and cause the WFOE to pay dividends into it. Personal civil asset restitution, blacklisting, travel bans, and criminal prosecution for defrauding the revenue under the Criminal Law are all available sanctions. The corporate veil will be pierced where the shell arrangement lacks economic substance and is used to evade mandatory tax obligations.
